message:
docs(test): say what the shipped-helper gate cannot see

Test 1, comments only. Asked for by the reviewer, and right to ask.

The gate matches a list of patterns. A switch named something not on that list walks straight past
it, and the list cannot be completed -- there is no enumeration of every name a hidden argument
might take. A green run here is therefore weaker evidence than it looks, and the test now says so
in the place someone reads before trusting it.

The argument it corroborates is structural, not statistical: the stall is reached by swapping the
file the host resolves as its helper, so the product needs no such argument and parses none. That
is checkable by reading parse_args rather than by scanning bytes -- grep for test, stall, fault or
inject across gdi_capture_worker_main.cpp returns zero. The scan is the cheap thing that would
notice if that stopped being true by accident.

Also recorded: it reads two executables. GNLinkCapture because it is the helper, GNLinkStream
because that is where the kill is linked and therefore the only place the fault translation unit
could land. Anything shipped that is neither is not covered, and saying that is cheaper than
leaving a reader to assume otherwise.

19 of 19, twice.
